You can check the MCP startup log directly:

```
! cat ~/.claude/logs/mcp-server-claude-context.log 2>/dev/null | tail -30
```

Run that (with `!` to keep output in chat) and it'll show the actual error. If the file doesn't exist, Claude Code never even tried to launch it — that would point to a settings parse issue instead.
